title: Lacks basic UX
body:
I’ve tried a mix of similar org app’s, along with paper options. After reading Get Things Done, I was motivated to try again. As an Outlook user this seemed logical.

The Good: so far it’s the best I have found. I’m using it and generally pleased. That’s saying something.

The Bad: very simple UX elements are inconsistent, missing or don’t function as inferred. These are very bad and thus simple (and simply unnecessary). First, starting a new title of a List or Group or Task should always delete the default name in one press of the backspace. In some it does, in others it doesn’t. That’s stupid.

Second, when typing the name of a new Task, List or Group, it should always default to a capitalized first letter. Again, on some it does and others it does not. Once more: stupid.

Lastly, adding a List inside a Group requires an added step. It’s not an easy option. Rather the new List must first be generically added, and then dragged to the intended Group. That’s a PITN and unnecessary. 

Please resolve these simple UX flaws to further improve the app. It’s pretty good but feels rough around the edges as is. I am using the latest version for Apple OS on an iPhone.

title: App Crashes On iOS devices
body:
I’ve been a long-time user of Microsoft To Do across different platforms, and while it works flawlessly on Android and Windows, the iOS version has become nearly unusable due to a major issue.

After launching the app on my iPhone, it crashes within 1–2 minutes, abruptly closing and returning me to the main menu/home screen. Worse, this crash seems to cause temporary instability in the overall iOS system — other apps freeze or hang briefly, and the device becomes sluggish for a few seconds after the crash. This goes beyond a minor bug and feels like it’s affecting the core performance of iOS itself.

In contrast, the app performs smoothly on Android and Windows, syncing tasks as expected and delivering the productivity support I rely on. The cross-platform experience would be great if not for the iOS-specific issues.

I hope Microsoft addresses this bug soon, as it significantly impacts usability for iPhone users and undermines trust in an otherwise reliable productivity tool.

title: Refuses to sync and crashes
body:
Applications created to help people track their tasks must have only one property which trumps everything else - reliability. As of version 2.140 this app does not have any.
1. It crashes frequently, seemingly when it tries to sync. 
2. Sometimes it doesn't crash but does not sync either. Sync status in the main menu says "Up to Date" but it is not - frequently it shows obsolete state of the tasks which may be a few days old. Attempt to force sync by taping on "Up to Date" does not help.
3. Even when everything  works as designed when you start the app it shows some obsolete state and then after 10-20-30 seconds it refreshes. There is no visual indication if it already refreshed or not so one has to guess. And if you guess wrong you end up editing something which may not even exist anymore.
4. There is no way to submit feedback or debug logs from the app. No way to contact support either. Whom are they hiding from?

To me this app is at the bottom of the ToDo apps pile because of how unreliable and frustrating it is to use every single time.

title: Has so much potential, but falls short
body:
This app could be the best to-do list app on the market, but it needs improvements on simple things.

1) You cannot collapse pictures attached to a task, it simply uses up tons of real estate on the screen with the attached picture.

2) There’s no way to manually sort/prioritize tasks added to the “Important” list.

3) For some reason, manually rearranging tasks in lists that allow it is physically cumbersome. Often times if you don’t place the task just right in the GUI, it will be pulled off the list, sorted elsewhere, or the app will not allow you to move it. Considering rearranging tasks is an integral part of task management, this seriously hinders productivity. It’s annoying at best, and makes the app almost unusable at worst.

4) Unable to assign sub-tasks to “My Day” or “Important” lists. This forces the user to drill down into the list instead of seeing which subtask needs to be accomplished at a glance.

There are other issues, but alas I must actually get things done before heading back to work tomorrow.

There are also quite a few QoL improvements that could be made, like not putting the same item in a list multiple times.

title: Add a layer of hierarchy to prioritization
body: High, medium, low, is not sufficient. The app needs an additional level of hierarchy so that users can identify lists of one through N for each high, medium and low prioritized accordingly. This capability was available in tasks in Outlook with some minor customization. Bring it back.

title: It Crashes—A lot.
body: This app would be a 5 if it didn’t crash every 30 seconds. I continuously have to reopen the app to enter info. I keep it because I use other Microsoft products and I like how they integrate, so I’m not ready to give up on it yet. But this issue does need to be fixed. Especially if so many people have brought it to your attention.
